thread:
tom: FYI seeing intermittent test failures in the JS SDK sample when running Vitest in CI with type: "module". Locally OK. Anyone seen ESM mock flakiness?
anya: Yep. CI log shows `TypeError: (0 , _inference.createClient) is not a function` and other runs show `ERR_REQUIRE_ESM`.
kevin: Two layers: (1) test runner transform/prebundle changes module shape, (2) Jest will `require()` ESM-only packages and explode.
tom: Our tests import default: `import inference from '@redwood/inference'` but many mocks use named shapes.
anya: Short-term: change tests to named imports or make mocks preserve __esModule: `vi.mock('@redwood/inference', async () => { const real = await vi.importActual('@redwood/inference'); return { __esModule: true, ...real, createClient: () => ({ predict: () => 'ok' }) } })`. That fixed my local flake.
kevin: For Vitest config add `test: { environment: 'edge-runtime', deps: { inline: ['@redwood/inference'] } }` and `resolve: { conditions: ['import'] }`. For Jest add `transformIgnorePatterns: ['/node_modules/(?!@redwood/inference)']` or publish a CJS entry.
tom: TS in the test runner complained about missing declarations. I added `test/types.d.ts` with `declare module '@redwood/inference';` and included it in tsconfig.test.json. Quieted the compiler.
anya: Long-term fix is on SDK side: publish dual ESM/CJS bundles, include dist/index.d.ts, and add an exports map so node/jest/vite resolve correctly.
ci-bot: Opened issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/issues/547 (vitest/jest ESM mock flake) with repro and logs.
tom: I'll add a Troubleshooting blurb to the sample-app README with the vitest snippet and the mock shim. Putting a link to #547. Keeping issue open until SDK release. :+1:
